hints.title: Manhattan Distance Dimension Independence
hints.text: The total Manhattan distance is the sum of row distances plus column distances, allowing optimal coordinates to be solved independently per axis.

hints.title: Median Minimizes One-Dimensional Distance Sum
hints.text: In one dimension, the point that minimizes sum of distances to a collection of points is their median value.

hints.title: Collecting Sorted Coordinates and Inward Pair Summation
hints.text: Collect row indices of all ones (naturally sorted), and collect column indices (sort them). For each list, sum distances between outer pairs using inward pointers.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(M * N) time when columns are gathered by column traversal, or O(K log K) where K is number of homes.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating distance from all M * N grid cells takes O((M * N)^2) operations.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Decomposing 2D grid into two 1D coordinate projections isolates the median search.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that Manhattan distance separates cleanly into two 1D L1-median optimization subproblems.
